mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW Z8 4.9 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW Z8 4.9 engine replacement typically costs £12,000-£18,000 supply-only for rebuilt units, or £14,000-£22,000 fitted by a specialist. The S62B50 is a specialist heritage engine requiring expert knowledge. Used S62B50 engines: £8,000-£14,000 supply-only. Reconditioned units: £12,000-£16,000 supply-only. Rebuilt units with upgraded components: £14,000-£18,000 supply-only. Professional fitting adds £2,000-£4,000 depending on workshop location.

mainEntity.name: What engine is fitted to the BMW Z8 4.9?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW Z8 4.9 is powered exclusively by the S62B50 4.9-litre V8 engine, developed by BMW Motorsport and shared with the E39 M5. Displacement: 4,941cc (4.9L). Power output: 394hp (400PS) @ 6,600rpm. Torque: 500Nm (369 lb-ft) @ 3,800rpm. Redline: 7,000rpm. Features: DOHC 32-valve, double-VANOS, individual throttle bodies.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW Z8 4.9 S62 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S62B50 has earned a reputation for reliability 'if maintained correctly'. However, it has well-documented weaknesses that are critical to address: Timing chain guides degrade over time - preventive replacement recommended around 100,000 miles. VANOS seals deteriorate, affecting performance. Cooling system components (water pump, thermostat) require regular inspection. Oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and oil filter housing are common.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain guide failure on a BMW Z8 4.9?

acceptedAnswer.text: The S62's timing chain guides are a known weakness: Rattling noise on cold start that may disappear as the engine warms. The plastic guides degrade over time due to heat cycling. If ignored, chain can jump causing catastrophic engine damage. Preventive replacement around 100,000 miles is strongly recommended.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a BMW Z8 4.9?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Z8 4.9 worth £100,000-£250,000+, a rebuilt S62B50 at £12,000-£18,000 can make excellent financial sense if the body, interior, and chassis are in good condition. Compare replacement cost against vehicle value - replacement is viable well beyond 70% of car's value for collector-grade examples. The Z8 'has become a collector's item', with values continuing to appreciate. Non-running Z8 chassis lose significant valuation versus documented, engine-ready examples. Always factor 12-month warranty and provenance documentation into replacement decision.

mainEntity.name: Can I use an E39 M5 S62 engine in my BMW Z8 4.9?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the S62B50 from an E39 M5 is the same basic engine used in the Z8. However, there are differences to be aware of: Z8-specific engine mounts and ancillaries are required. ECU calibration differs between E39 M5 and Z8 applications. Z8 semi-dry sump system may differ from M5 oiling setup. Always verify compatibility with a Z8 specialist before purchasing.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW Z8 4.9 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW Z8 (E52) is one of the most iconic and collectable roadsters ever built by BMW, produced from 1999 to 2003 with just 5,703 units manufactured. Designed as a homage to the legendary BMW 507, the Z8 was exclusively powered by the S62B50 4.9-litre V8 engine - developed by BMW Motorsport and shared with the E39 M5. With 394hp, individual throttle bodies, and a 7,000rpm redline, the S62 remains one of the greatest naturally aspirated V8 engines ever produced.

milestones.description: Z8 production begins with S62B50 4.9L V8, 394hp, 6-speed manual transmission
Full production model launched; all-aluminium chassis and body
2003 - S62B50 remains the sole engine for standard Z8 production
Alpina Z8 Roadster V8 introduced with 4.8L M62 V8, 375hp, 5-speed automatic
End of production; 5,703 Z8s built in total

commonProblems.h2: BMW Z8 4.9 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW Z8 4.9's S62B50 V8 is one of BMW M's greatest naturally aspirated engines, but as these cars approach 25+ years of age, predictable wear patterns emerge - timing chain guide degradation, VANOS seal failure, and cooling system issues being the most significant. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address these original failure points - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW Z8 4.9's S62 V8 Rattles on Start-Up
problems.rootCause: The S62 uses plastic timing chain guides that degrade over time due to heat cycling and age. When the guides fail, the timing chain can become loose, causing rattling on start-up and, if ignored, potential catastrophic engine failure. As one expert notes: "Preventive replacement around 100,000 miles (160,000 km) is recommended".

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain guides, tensioner, chain, and sprockets
Supply & fit rebuilt S62B50 with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW Z8 4.9 is worth £100,000-£250,000+ depending on condition, mileage, and provenance. Low-mileage, well-documented examples can command significantly more. Given the vehicle's collector-car status and appreciating value, engine replacement is generally viable for well-maintained examples. As one source notes, the Z8 "has become a collector's item".
problems.recommendation: On any Z8 4.9 without documented timing chain guide work within the last 80,000 miles, preventative guide and tensioner replacement is strongly advised. A £2,200-£3,500 specialist chain guide kit is far cheaper than a £12,000+ engine rebuild. Once the chain jumps, the engine is almost certainly damaged.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt S62B50 engine prices for your BMW Z8 4.9

problems.h4: VANOS Seal Failure - Why the BMW Z8 4.9 Loses Low-End Power
problems.rootCause: The S62 was BMW's first V8 engine with double-VANOS - variable valve timing on both intake and exhaust camshafts. The VANOS seals degrade over time, causing a loss of low-end torque, rough idle, and reduced fuel economy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace VANOS seals with upgraded Viton units, reset timing
repairOptions.longevity: Restores factory power delivery; 60,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete VANOS unit overhaul, new solenoids and oil lines
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if internal wear is significant

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt S62B50 with upgraded VANOS components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if VANOS failure caused timing chain damage

problems.recommendation: VANOS seal failure on the S62 is a well-understood issue. Specialist seal replacement using upgraded Viton seals costs under £1,200 and restores factory power delivery. This is almost always the right first step - a full engine replacement is rarely necessary unless the engine has suffered catastrophic failure.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW Z8 4.9 Overheats
problems.rootCause: Like other BMW engines of the era, the S62's cooling system components (radiators, water pumps, expansion tanks) degrade over time. The water pump and thermostat can fail, leading to overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, expansion tank, hoses, coolant flush
Head skim, pressure test, new head gasket, cooling system overhaul
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if block and bottom end remain undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt S62B50 with upgraded cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if overheating caused cracked block or scored bores

problems.recommendation: On any Z8 4.9 without documented cooling system work, proactive replacement of the water pump, thermostat, and expansion tank is essential. A £700-£1,200 specialist overhaul is far cheaper than a £12,000+ engine rebuild. Check coolant levels regularly.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW Z8 4.9 cooling system repair costs

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Why the BMW Z8 4.9 Drips Oil
problems.rootCause: The S62 is prone to oil leaks, particularly around the valve cover gaskets and oil filter housing. These gaskets become brittle with age and heat cycling.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets and/or oil filter housing gasket
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; 50,000+ mile lifespan

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt S62B50 with new gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation caused bearing damage

problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on the S62 are common but rarely catastrophic if addressed promptly. Check for oil around the valve covers and oil filter housing regularly. A £350-£650 specialist gasket replacement is cheap insurance against a more serious oil starvation issue.
problems.cta: -> Compare BMW Z8 4.9 oil leak repair costs
